title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 42
paragraphs: When he expressed this judgment, no one opposed him, and so his opinion prevailed; for it was he, and not Artabazos, who had been given command of the army by the king. He therefore summoned the commanders of the divisions and the generals of the Greeks with him, and asked whether they knew of any oracle about the Persians that said they were destined to be destroyed in Greece. Those summoned to council fell silent, some not knowing the oracles and others knowing them but thinking it unsafe to speak; then Mardonius himself said: “Since you either know nothing or do not venture to speak, I will tell you, for I know very well. There is an oracle saying that the Persians are destined, when they come to Greece, to plunder the temple at Delphi, and having plundered it to perish, every one of them. We, therefore, precisely because we know this, will not go to that temple, nor will we attempt to plunder it; and for this reason we shall not perish. So those of you who happen to wish well to the Persians, rejoice so far as this matter is concerned, and be assured that we shall overcome the Greeks.” Having spoken to them thus, he next commanded them to prepare everything and set all in order, since at dawn of the next day a battle would be fought.
